claims.statement: JUCE Normalise is energy-based (0.125 / sqrt(hottest-channel-energy)) — used for reverb IRs so an IR's absolute level means nothing. Short IRs (≤ 1 s, cab class) instead get a −18 dB output pad (computeIrNormalizationGain) with 100% default mix; long IRs (> 1 s, reverb class) use Normalise with 50% default mix. kMaxIrSeconds = 10.0 is a hard cap on loaded IR length; kShortIrMaxBaseSamples = 48000 (1 s at the 48 kHz base rate); kLongIrDefaultMix = 0.5.

The IR convolver runs at the base (chain) rate, NOT the host rate: IR blocks are rate-isolated islands inside the 48 kHz chain domain (ChainDomain's boundary resampler re-samples host↔chain at the chain edges). This is why BudgetConvolver's sample-count constants (kFrame=8192, kMaxCall=256) refer to 48 kHz samples even when the host runs 96/192 kHz — the convolver never sees host-rate samples.

BudgetConvolver (plugin/include/effects/conv/BudgetConvolver.h; formerly flat plugin/include/BudgetConvolver.h before the per-effect subdirectory move) is a bounded per-call OLA long-tail convolver: it does the same per-pair math as JUCE's non-uniform engine (real-only FFT 16384, verbatim JUCE packed-domain product: prepareForConvolution / convolutionProcessingAndAccumulate / updateSymmetricFrequencyDomainData) — the difference is schedule. JUCE (processSamplesWithAddedLatency) pays FWD FFT + all N outstanding (frame×seg) products + IFFT in ONE boundary call once per 8192 input samples — worse the longer the IR; BudgetConvolver pays one 16384-point real transform + one new (frame×seg0) product in one call, defers the IFFT to the NEXT call, and bounds steady-state calls to K old products (K = ceil(M / callsMax), M = tailSamples/8192 + 1). Heaviest call ≈ one 16384-pt real transform (~0.35 ms 2-ch), well under 1.0 ms.

kIrConvolverMaxBlockSize = 256 (ChainBlock.h) caps the per-call BudgetConvolver feed; irConvolverBlockSizeFor and processConvolverInChunks (ChainBlock.h) split any host-sized block into ≤256-sample slices so per-call OLA product cost cannot inflate with the host's block size — the host block may be larger than the cap but the product budget per call stays bounded regardless. BudgetConvolver.h (now in plugin/include/effects/conv/) carries the matching kMaxCall = 256 / kFrame = 8192 pair as its own copy of the house CPU law (ConvolutionReverb.h references this cap in its header comment: 'Block-size cap (kIrConvolverMaxBlockSize) + chunked RT feed').

The conv wet path ends in a stateless soft-knee peak limiter (process stage 3c, ConvolutionReverb.cpp:845-849, gated by clipEnabled_, NOT applied on the dying crossfade tail): a 1024-entry LUT over log|x| in [kClipLogLo=-6.9, kClipLogHi=5.3], law H(u) = 2.2886 + (-5.1009*u - 9.6838)*T with T = smoothstep((u + 1.4498)/4.4287) — floor lift kClipFloorDb=2.2886 dB at low levels, knee at x≈kClipKneeX=0.2231, ceiling kClipCeilingGain=1.3232 (1/|x| roll above it). The LUT is filled with juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain (a plain e^(db/20) fill is a constant -1.29 dB bug). No user knob, not part of state, and deliberately EXCLUDED from IR export. Law guarded by WetClipCurveLaw + WetClipInPath in test/src/convolution_reverb_tests.cpp (plain 0.3 dB tolerance); the 7 pre-clip contract tests call setClipEnabledForTest(false).

Mod layer soft clip (commit 9a5c3c8, spec spc-1792538043915-13755; supersedes the 44a78ea one-pole wet-ring write-tau, which lowpassed the modulated layer to ~silence — +0.00 dB measured at mod 1.0): the wet RING WRITE is raw again, and a tanh soft clip is applied to the ADDED MOD LAYER ONLY (never the wet itself) before it is summed in: `lay = cl * tanh(lay / cl)` with `cl = kModClipScale = 1e-2` (ConvolutionReverb.h:172), site ConvolutionReverb.cpp:782-790,828. Zero-latency and stateless; mod 1.0 = +1.00 dB layer measured and the ship clip cuts the burst click hunt >2× (derivative RMS). `setModClipScaleForTest(scale)` (h:320): <0 = linear (bit-exact anchor for the contract tests), 0 = ship kModClipScale, >0 = explicit. Guarded by ConvolutionReverb.ModLayerClipClickHunt + ModClipDisabledIsBitExact (test/src/convolution_reverb_tests.cpp); DspTests 581/581.

Per-IR trim cap + on-load reset (commit 9a5c3c8, specs spc-1792564638419-71605 + spc-1792565053306-88633): the Start/End UI faces use `scales::convTrimScale(rawSeconds)` (plugin/ui/core/KnobScale.h:675) — linear 0..cap in seconds, cap = raw IR length rounded up to whole seconds (sub-second IRs get a 1 s face; caches per whole-second cap), so a window can never point past a short IR's tail and silently keep serving the old engine (empty trim window = silent no-op, A5). The raw length rides the chain state as `convRawSeconds` (all state places). ON IR LOAD, TONE3000Processor::loadConvIr (ProcessorChain.cpp:479-481, before setParams) resets the window to the full span and the stretch to 1.00×: convStartS = 0.0, convEndS = block->conv.rawSeconds(), convPitch = 0.5. Guarded by ProcessorTest.ConvIrLoadResetsTrimWindowAndTime (test/src/processor_tests.cpp) + ConvTrimScaleTest.CapIsRawLengthRoundedUp (test/src/effect_ui_scale_tests.cpp).

ConvolutionReverb (IR-driven plate reverb; plugin/include/effects/conv/ConvolutionReverb.h) shares this engine: a ~150 ms install-fade warmup (JUCE's dry crossfade elapses off the live path by feeding the fresh tail one silence frame at rebuild — ConvolutionReverb.cpp ~325-327, `cold.clear()` then `tail->process(cold)` — not at first wet; the dedicated message-thread `primeSilence` warm-up was removed in the 2026-10-20 optimization-findings Stage 5 as a zero-caller), and the JUCE non-uniform OLA replaced by the BudgetConvolver tail. Reverb-specific: user time-stretch (JUCE re-samples the edited IR to engine rate), 4.0 quad→stereo downmix folded BEFORE JUCE sees it (L=(c0+c2)/√2, R=(c1+c3)/√2 — JUCE reads only ch 0/1 and would drop the rear pair), and JUCE Normalise on the load path. The mod layer writes the wet ring RAW (the 44a78ea one-pole write-tau was removed at 9a5c3c8 — it lowpassed the layer to ~silence; the click fix is now a tanh soft clip on the added layer only, see the mod claim).

The conv wet path ends in a stateless soft-knee peak limiter (process stage 3c, ConvolutionReverb.cpp:847-856, gated by clipEnabled_, NOT applied on the dying crossfade tail): a 1024-entry LUT over log|x| in [kClipLogLo=-6.9, kClipLogHi=5.3], law H(u) = 2.2886 + (-5.1009*u - 9.6838)*T with T = smoothstep((u + 1.4498)/4.4287) — floor lift kClipFloorDb=2.2886 dB at low levels, knee at x≈kClipKneeX=0.2231, ceiling kClipCeilingGain=1.3232 (1/|x| roll above it). The LUT is filled with juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain (a plain e^(db/20) fill is a constant -1.29 dB bug). No user knob, not part of state, and deliberately EXCLUDED from IR export. Law guarded by WetClipCurveLaw + WetClipInPath in test/src/convolution_reverb_tests.cpp (plain 0.3 dB tolerance); the 7 pre-clip contract tests call setClipEnabledForTest(false).

Kernel export (commit 89afb4e): ConvolutionReverb::exportKernel(targetRate, &error) (ConvolutionReverb.h:372, cpp:390) re-runs the SAME makeEditedState linear pipeline — trim (convStartS/convEndS) + stretch (Time) + fades/curves — at the raw file rate, then resamples to the target rate and bakes the linear stages: Pre zero-pad, Gain (pow(10, gainToDb/20)), Width (stereo M/S fold; mono IR = Haas interaural delay pair, kHaasDelayMs, side = width*kHaasDepth*delayed). Mod and the wet soft clip are live-only and deliberately not baked. The result is always 2-channel (mono duplicated). TONE3000Processor::exportConvIr (ProcessorChain.cpp:488) wraps it: bits clamped 16..32, WavAudioFormat writer over a file OutputStream (the juce::MemoryOutputStream 0-byte trap class), deletes the file on failure. Guarded by ConvIrExport* tests (convolution_reverb_tests.cpp) + the exportConvIr WAV round-trip (processor_tests.cpp).

Mod layer soft clip + tap smoothing (commits 9a5c3c8 + 2b04a71; supersedes the 44a78ea one-pole wet-ring write-tau, which lowpassed the modulated layer to ~silence): the wet RING WRITE is raw (wr[w] = wet[i], cpp:809), and TWO protections apply to the ADDED MOD LAYER ONLY (never the wet itself): (1) a one-pole lowpass on the LAYER SUM with kModTapTauMs=5.0 (ConvolutionReverb.h:189, site cpp:829-834 `modSumSm_[c] = a*modSumSm_[c] + (1.0-a)*sum`) — tames the re-emitted transient edges the wobbled taps pick up; the 1 Hz LFO body is far below the ~32 Hz corner; tau==0 → alpha 0 → raw sum (bit-exact anchor); (2) a tanh soft clip on the layer AFTER the one-pole: `wet[i] += cl * tanh(lay/cl)` with cl = kModClipScale = 1e-1 (ConvolutionReverb.h:179, site cpp:837-838). Zero-latency, causal. `setModClipScaleForTest(scale)` (h:337): <0 = linear (bit-exact anchor), 0 = ship kModClipScale, >0 = explicit; `modTapTauForTest()` (h:339) reads back the active tau; `zeroModStageForTest()` (h:343) zeros modBuf_/modPh_/modW_/modSumSm_ for shared-baseline law tests. Guarded by 4 tests: ModLayerClipClickHunt (crest law 0.95×), ModClipDisabledIsBitExact, ModTapSmoothingLaw (shared-baseline HF + burst-body laws), TwoFreshEnginesSameModLayer (fresh-engine comparability, factor ≤ 10). DspTests 584/584.
